Hi Elena / Wayfinder procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion I wanted to put a concrete commercial framing on the table so your procurement and finance teams can run the numbers. Key points up front:
- We can offer a bundled on‑prem (VPC) SKU that combines the platform license + 24x7 support at the Enterprise tier.
- To address your migration runway ask, we can front‑load a timebound credit that offsets the platform fee for Year 1 (applied as invoice credits).

Markus — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. A few clarifying items from procurement/finance:

* We prefer credits that show on invoices (not amortized in the SOW) — simpler for auditors.
* Our finance team is sensitive to platform fee waivers that extend beyond 12 months; a one‑year runway credit gets easier buy‑in.
* We need a breakdown that separates the platform license (recurring) from the engineering onboarding retainer (one‑time).

Also: can you do an alternative that reduces the upfront platform fee by 25% in Year 1 instead of a full credit? That would be a helpful counter‑offer to present to our CFO.

We'll also need the final SOW to include an invoice schedule aligned to our fiscal quarter. Happy to share a sample PO template if it helps.

—Elena

Marissa / Neha — forwarding Elena's reply. Two asks:

1) Can we structure a 12‑month timebound credit equal to 25% of Year 1 platform fees (applied as invoice credits) and still keep the net ARR economics acceptable? The customer specifically asked for a scaled reduction rather than a full waiver.
2) If we do the 25% credit, finance will want a conditional clause: if they expand capacity above the committed baseline within 9 months, we prorate and invoice the delta. Need standard language.

Also, can we trade down 50 hours of onboarding engineering (from our migration retainer) in lieu of additional cash credit if that preserves margin? Elena indicated service credits might move approvals faster.

If you can sketch two small options (25% invoice credit vs 15% + 50 onboarding hours) I can present both to Elena this week.

Thanks — Markus

Hey team — quick take from pricing/finance:

- 25% invoice credit on Year 1 platform fees is doable as a limited, one‑time credit. Finance prefers the credit to be explicitly timebound (12 months) and tied to invoice line items.
- We should avoid conditional proration language that requires frequent reconciliations; instead, include a one‑time true‑up within 90 days if committed capacity changes >20% from the baseline. That keeps book closing predictable.
- 50 hours of onboarding (service credit) is an acceptable swap if we cap the usage to 6 months post‑go‑live; mark as non‑transferable.

I've attached the support_ladder.pdf with the Enterprise tier commitments and SLAs; include the oncall escalation hours in the SOW.

I'll draft two short commercial bullets for the SOW:
A) 25% invoice credit on Year 1 platform fees; one‑time true‑up within 90 days if committed capacity changes >20%.
B) 15% invoice credit on Year 1 platform fees + 50 onboarding hours (use within 6 months).

Ping me if you want the exact line‑level wording.

—Neha

Hi Elena — appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on procurement feedback and internal pricing options, here are two clean options for your CFO to evaluate. Both are structured to appear as invoice credits (per your auditor preference) and aligned to a 12‑month timebound runway: 

Option 1 (Simple credit):
- 25% invoice credit on Year 1 platform fees (applied as line item credits across the first four invoices).
- One‑time true‑up within 90 days if committed capacity at go‑live is >20% different from the baseline.
- SOW will separate the recurring platform license from the onboarding retainer; invoicing schedule aligned to Wayfinder fiscal quarter.

Option 2 (Credit + services):
- 15% invoice credit on Year 1 platform fees.
- 50 onboarding hours (non‑transferable), use within 6 months post‑go‑live; tracked against the migration retainer.
- Same true‑up language as Option 1.
